result.summary: Do not dispatch yet: the revised classification still labels potentially irreversible deletion as lossless housekeeping.

findings.title: Class C treats unproven or unequal copies as safe duplicates
findings.body: O1 includes failed identity reads and differing buffers in class C, then asserts that these files cannot be only-copies. validate.js:1489–1504 deliberately retains those files because equivalence is unproven. Executing that identity branch and the actual prune against an in-memory filesystem with unequal copies retained both initially, then destroyed the redacted version while the different withheld version survived. O2 and O8 incorrectly describe this outcome as 'no loss' and use it to justify the retention decision. The class-A-only test cannot expose this error.
findings.recommendation: Separate proven duplicates whose cleanup failed from unequal or unreadable copies. Treat the latter as potentially sole-surviving versions, correct the dependent decisions and owner-item wording, and require regression coverage for unequal-copy and identity-read-failure cases.

next_steps: Correct the classification and dependent loss claims before closing the design gate.
